bib.title: Describe Anything: Detailed Localized Image and Video Captioning

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Describe Anything: Detailed Localized Image and Video Captioning" (DAM). Long Lian, Yifan Ding, Yunhao Ge, Sifei Liu, Hanzi Mao, Boyi Li, Marco Pavone, Ming-Yu Liu, Trevor Darrell, Adam Yala, Yin Cui (NVIDIA, UC Berkeley, UCSF). arXiv:2504.16072v1, preprint, 22 Apr 2025.

COVERAGE: 32 of 32 pages. About 113k chars of ~133k read (all body and appendices A-H, the tables, the prompt in Table A.7, the start of the references). The rest is the reference list (skimmed) and the last part of H.3 (inference setting, prompt-augmentation detail). Text extraction was clean, apart from ligature glitches in the figure text.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- DAM, a 3B model, beats GPT-4o, o1 and all region-specific VLMs on DLC-Bench, the paper's own benchmark.
  number: 67.3% average (52.3 pos / 82.2 neg) for DAM-3B. GPT-4o 61.5. o1 62.5. Claude 3.7 Sonnet 36.1. Gemini 2.5 Pro 55.8. VP-SPHINX 13B (cropped input) 49.0. Qwen2.5-VL 7B 41.2.
  setup: Detailed localized captioning on 892 questions from Objects365 v2 val. A text-only Llama 3.1 8B judge scores the captions. General VLMs were prompted with the same cropped+masked prompt used in data-pipeline stage 1.
  quote: "DAM (Ours) 3B 52.3 82.2 67.3" and "GPT-4o [54] - 43.4 79.6 61.5" and "o1 [55]† - 46.3 78.8 62.5"
  where: Table 5, p.8
- The focal prompt (full image plus an expanded crop, each with a mask) with gated cross-attention drives the gain, with no extra LLM vision tokens.
  number: Full image only 48.7%, local crop only 60.1%, naive full+crop concatenation 42.4% (392 image tokens), full+crop with cross-attention 63.2%, focal crop only 65.4%, full+focal crop with cross-attention 67.3% (196 image tokens).
  setup: DLC-Bench, 3B, image-only training, trained on the same data.
  quote: "Full + Focal CropYes 196 52.3 82.2 67.3 (+18.6)" and "Simply concatenating both performs poorly (42.4%)."
  where: Table 8, p.10
- The same data on a different architecture gives much less, so the architecture matters and not only the data.
  number: VP-SPHINX architecture 50.2% vs DAM architecture 63.8%.
  setup: VP-SPHINX trained on the DLC-SDP data. DLC-Bench average.
  quote: "Avg (%) 50.2 63.8"
  where: Table A.1, p.9
- Data scaling and SSL both help.
  number: LVIS-only 373k regions 53.3%. Adding datasets (602k regions) 63.8%. Adding SSL on 10% of SA-1B (1.38M regions) 67.3%.
  setup: DLC-Bench average.
  quote: "+ SSL on 10% of SA-1B 1.38M 52.3 82.2 67.3 (+14.0)"
  where: Table 9, p.10
- Keyword-level SOTA on PACO and LVIS.
  number: PACO semantic IoU 73.2% and semantic similarity 84.2%, beating the previous best by 23.2% and 8.5%. LVIS 89.0 / 77.7.
  setup: Open-class keyword captioning. Previous best VP-LLAVA-8B on PACO: 75.7 / 50.0.
  quote: "our method achieves 73.2% semantic IoU and 84.2% semantic similarity, outperforming the previous best by 23.2% and 8.5% respectively."
  where: Table 2, p.7-8
- Phrase-level, zero-shot on Flickr30k Entities: 12.3% average relative gain over the previous best.
  number: CIDEr 74.7 vs 67.4 for VP-SPHINX-13B.
  quote: "outperforming the previous best by 12.3% relative improvement on an average of 5 metrics."
  where: Table 3, p.8
- Detailed captioning on Ref-L4 (Objects365 split, zero-shot).
  number: 33.4% average relative gain on short-caption metrics, 13.1% on long-caption metrics (CLAIR 57.9 vs 51.2).
  setup: Predictions and references were summarized with GPT-4o-mini before the short metrics. CLAIR was run on raw outputs.
  quote: "33.4% relative improvement on average over the previous best on short language-based captioning metrics"
  where: Table 4, p.8
- Video, HC-STVG: 19.8% relative improvement over the previous best.
  number: CIDEr 91.0 vs VideoRefer-7B 68.6. BLEU@4 19.8.
  setup: DAM-8B.
  quote: "our proposed DAM achieves 19.8% relative improvement over the previous best on HC-STVG"
  where: Table 6, p.8
- VideoRefer-Bench-D, 1-5 scale from a GPT-4o judge.
  number: Zero-shot average 3.34 (GPT-4o 3.25). In-domain average 3.68 (VideoRefer-7B 3.46). On the hallucination-detection (HD) sub-task, zero-shot DAM scores 2.58, GPT-4o 2.43, and Elysium-7B 3.59.
  quote: "DAM-8B (Ours) 4.45 3.30 3.03 2.58 3.34"
  where: Table 7, p.9
- Reference-caption benchmarks wrongly punish correct extra detail, which is the motive for DLC-Bench.
  number: none
  quote: "the metrics from the benchmark will treat the correct details in the caption prediction about the region of interest that are not mentioned in the ground truth reference caption as hallucinations."
  where: App. C.2, p.4 of the appendix
- Training and efficiency are cheap.
  number: ~1.5M training samples (1.46M regions over 819k images). The vision encoder adds 0.06s latency vs 1.49s for the 3B LLM (400M vs 3B/8B parameters). Training took under a day: 8 A100s for 3B, 32 A100s for 8B.
  setup: Fine-tuned from VILA 1.5 with a SigLIP encoder, 1 epoch, batch size 2048.
  quote: "minimal latency impact (0.06s compared to 1.49s for 3B LLM as measured in our pipeline)"
  where: App. C.5, H.2
- Set-of-Marks prompting is much worse than the stage-1 prompt for off-the-shelf VLMs.
  number: GPT-4o (SoM) 17.1 avg, Gemini 2.5 Pro (SoM) 39.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet (SoM) 20.4, VILA1.5 3B (SoM) 7.5 (Pos -0.4).
  setup: DLC-Bench average.
  quote: "GPT-4o (SOM) [54] - 5.0 29.2 17.1"
  where: Table A.4
- Region-specific VLMs often do no better than generic VLMs on DLC-Bench.
  number: e.g. Shikra 22.2 (full) and 29.7 (cropped) average.
  quote: "Interestingly, region-specific VLMs often perform on par or worse than generic VLMs."
  where: App. C.7
- Joint image+video training is slightly better than image-only. Prompt augmentation costs a little.
  number: 68.9 vs 67.3 average (neg 85.4 vs 82.2). With prompt augmentation 66.7 vs 67.3.
  quote: "Image+Video Joint Training 52.4 85.4 68.9"
  where: Tables A.2, A.3. Note that the 3B model is used for both rows.
- Zero-shot regional QA and 3D object captioning work without any training on them (qualitative only).
  number: none
  quote: "DAM surprisingly exhibits emerging zero-shot capabilities on regional QA."
  where: App. G.2, Fig. A.6. Co3Dv2 in Fig. 6b.

Method details
- Focal prompt: take the mask's bounding box and expand it by alpha=3, giving up to 9x the area. Enforce a minimum of 48 px. Use the full image and the crop, each with its mask.
- Localized vision backbone: a zero-initialized mask patch embedding, plus gated cross-attention adapters (tanh gates initialized to 0) in the regional encoder. The regional encoder shares weights with the global encoder.
- Video: frame features are concatenated along the sequence, and SAM 2 propagates sparse prompts into per-frame masks. Videos are treated as 8 images, following VILA 1.5.
- DLC-SDP stage 1: a VLM expands human-annotated mask+keyword pairs into detailed captions. The keyword is not given to DAM as input.
  - Stage 1 data: LVIS, Mapillary Vistas, COCO Stuff, OpenImages v7 and PACO. 684k regions over 226k images in the Table A.5 caption, or "603k regions across 202k images" in H.1 text (the two numbers are inconsistent).
- DLC-SDP stage 2 (SSL): OWL-ViT v2 proposals, SAM masks, SigLIP/CLIP confidence filtering, DAM self-labeling, then data expansion. It uses 10% of SA-1B (774k regions) and SA-V for video (94k regions over 37k videos).
- DLC-Bench scoring: positive questions give +1 for a correct detail, 0.5 for partial, 0 for omitted and -1 for a factual error. Negative questions give +1 for correctly omitting a detail and a penalty for including it. Points are only awarded if the object is recognised.
- The judge is Llama 3.1 8B. Question drafts came from GPT-4o (34 regions), Gemini 1.5 Pro (35) and Claude 3.5 Sonnet (31), then were manually curated.

LIMITS
- Concession (C.4): DAM is trained only for multi-granular localized captioning and is "not specifically optimized for other general vision-language tasks".
- Failure cases (C.3, Fig. A.4): it misrecognizes a frog-shaped slipper as a frog. It is confused by combined object and camera motion. The authors say "We expect these errors to be mitigated by broader data coverage."
- Weak on the video hallucination-detection sub-task zero-shot. The authors attribute this to incomplete reference captions rather than hallucination, based on one qualitative example (Fig. A.3), not a quantitative analysis.
- The headline DLC-Bench comparison has several caveats:
  - The benchmark and the data pipeline are by the same authors.
  - The judge is a small text-only LLM (Llama 3.1 8B).
  - Baseline prompts used the authors' stage-1 prompt, and the baselines are not trained for this.
  - Thinking-mode models (o1, Claude 3.7, Gemini 2.5 Pro) were evaluated but not specially tuned.
  - Only 892 questions.
  - Benchmark questions were seeded by VLMs, including GPT-4o, which is also a baseline.
- Prompt augmentation was dropped for benchmark runs, and the ablation tables use the 3B image-only model.
- Mask input is required. Points and boxes depend on SAM and SAM 2 for conversion.
- The models are fine-tuned from VILA 1.5 (2024), and the baselines are 2024 to early 2025 models, so the comparisons have dated.
- The paper does not show any comparison on general VQA or reasoning tasks.

BUILDS ON
- VILA 1.5 (ref. [44]) with a SigLIP encoder (Zhai et al.) as the base VLM.
- Flamingo (Alayrac et al., 2022) and the gated cross-attention adapters of [1, 38].
- SAM (Kirillov et al.) and SAM 2 (Ravi et al., 2024), for mask conversion and video propagation.
- Self-training SSL: MixMatch (Berthelot et al., 2019) and ReMixMatch (Berthelot et al., 2019).
- OWL-ViT v2, for open-vocabulary detection.
- ShareGPT4V (Chen et al., 2023), mixed in to avoid forgetting.
- Set-of-Marks (Yang et al., [91]), as the baseline prompting approach.
- Comparison baselines:
  - VP-SPHINX/Visual Prompt (Lin et al., ref. [45]).
  - Osprey, Ferret, RegionGPT, GLaMM, Shikra, GPT4RoI.
  - VideoRefer, Artemis, Merlin.
- CLAIR (Chan et al., 2023), as an evaluation metric.
- Datasets: LVIS, PACO, Flickr30k Entities, Ref-L4, HC-STVG, SA-1B, SA-V.

CODE: no code in the paper. The only verbatim artefact is the stage-1 annotation prompt (Table A.7, p.16). Start: "You are responsible to write a very descriptive caption to describe the {{category}} in the provided SEGMENTED image. You may leverage the surrounding context of the SEGMENTED image provided in the CROPPED image." It then says "You must not mention any background...". The default inference prompt is "Describe the masked region in detail." (H.2). The authors state that code, models, data and benchmark are released at describe-anything.github.io.

FIGURES
- Fig. 2 (p.2): why previous region captioners lose detail, and why plain zooming loses context. It shows the problem in one glance.
- Fig. 3 (p.4): DAM architecture. A focal prompt of the full image + mask and a focal crop + mask goes through the localized vision backbone, with global features fed by gated cross-attention. This is the key diagram.
- Fig. 4 and Fig. A.5 (p.7 and A.5 on p.7 of the appendix): how the DLC-Bench judge works, with example positive and negative questions and their scores.
- Fig. 5 (p.9): qualitative comparison of region captions from DAM and baselines on a cucumber slice.
- Fig. A.1 (appendix p.2): four ways to localize (text, crop/mask, markers, separate mask input), showing why a separate mask input is best.
- Fig. A.2: ambiguity of boxes vs masks.
- Fig. A.3: a reference-caption evaluation that falsely flags a correct caption as hallucination.
- Fig. A.4: failure cases.
- Fig. A.11: video comparison against GPT-4o, Qwen2.5-VL and VideoRefer.
Figure captions were read from the extracted text. I did not run the figures script.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions in the PDF. Extraction was fine apart from garbled text inside figures and tables (ligatures, "ﬂ" glyphs) and missing spaces in some paragraphs. The text had a "Table 4" caption row split from its table. The paper's two numbers for stage-1 region counts disagree (603k/202k in H.1 vs 684k/226k in Table A.5 caption). I did not read the tail of H.3 (prompt-augmentation detail) or the reference list past the first entries. I saved the extraction at /tmp/dam.txt (an intermediate file, not a report).
